pull.title: feat(analytics): hide locally answered requests by default, and apply filters as they change
pull.body:
## What was wrong

The Analytics tab counted every request MCC answered itself alongside the ones that actually reached a provider. On this machine that is **1,336 of 14,662 rows (9%)** — 1,028 `probe_auto_response`, 278 `title_generation_skip`, 30 `suggestion_mode_skip`. They took most of the table's first page, sat in the provider breakdown as `answered locally · <rule>`, and were inside every card, chart and rate, so "how is my proxy doing upstream" could not be read off the tab without subtracting them by hand.

Second complaint, mechanical: a changed filter did nothing until **Apply** was clicked, so the numbers on screen routinely answered a question the controls no longer asked.

## Mechanism

Locally answered rows are exactly `provider IS NULL AND optimization IS NOT NULL`. `provider IS NULL AND optimization IS NULL` is the `(unknown)` case — a different claim — and stays visible. One `_where()` serves `list_requests`, `stats` and `pulse`, so a single predicate there covers the table, the cards, the series and model charts, the provider/key breakdowns, top errors, and the fallback/diverted routes at once.

## What the fix does

- New `local` filter: `all` / `hide` / `only`, on `_where`, `list_requests`, `stats`, `pulse` and the three admin routes (`/admin/api/requests`, `/stats`, `/pulse`). A fourth value is a **422**, matching how `status` is refused.
- **The API default stays `all`.** Absent means unfiltered, so exports, curl users, and the Guide's examples are unchanged. Only the dashboard prefers `hide`.
- `local` joins the stats cache-key tuple. Without it a `hide` call inside the 5 s TTL would be served the `all` numbers it had just cached, and the cards would contradict the table.
- New **Local answers** select (Hide / Show / Only) in the filter row, persisted in dashboard state and reset to Hide by **Clear filters**.
- **Filters apply themselves**: selects on `change`, text boxes 400 ms after the last keystroke, Enter still immediate, each from `offset = 0` and each persisted. **Apply** stays for people who would rather press it. `loadId` already discards stale responses, so overlapping loads from fast typing settle on the last one.
- One paragraph each in the in-dashboard Guide and `docs/USAGE.md`.

## Verification

Driven in Chrome against **this worktree's server on 8099**, over a `VACUUM INTO` copy of the real 14,662-row request log. The user's server on 8082 and `~/.fcc` were read-only throughout and never written.

```
local=       stats total   "answered locally" rows in table   provider breakdown keys
hide         13,326        0 of 25                            6 (no local:*)
all/absent   14,662        13 of 25                           9 (3 local:*)
only          1,336        25 of 25                           3 (all local:*)
nope         422 {"detail":"Invalid local filter"}
```

```
status -> error, no Apply click: one reload
  /admin/api/requests/stats?status=error&local=hide
  /admin/api/requests?limit=25&offset=0&status=error&local=hide   <- back to page 1
typing "time" in Search: 0 loads across four keystrokes, 1 after the pause
  /admin/api/requests/stats?status=error&q=time&local=hide
Clear filters: one reload, controls back to {local: hide, status: "", search: "", pageSize: 25},
  13,326 stored requests, 0 locally answered rows in the table
all -> hide -> all within 5 s: 14,662 / 13,326 / 14,662
auto-refresh: /admin/api/requests/pulse?local=only, 3 ticks, 0 spurious full reloads
F5 -> Local answers still "Only", 1,336 stored requests
console errors: none
```

**The cache question the spec asked to settle in the browser rather than with a bypass flag:** a different filter is a different key and therefore a miss by construction, and the only "hit" case (`all` again within 5 s) returned the correct 14,662. **No cache-bypass flag was added.**

```
$ uv run pytest -q --tb=line
15 failed, 7723 passed, 38 skipped in 102.45s

$ uv run ruff format && uv run ruff check && uv run ty check
990 files left unchanged / All checks passed! / All checks passed!

$ uv run pytest tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py -q
114 passed
```

The jsdom harness now drives the real `admin.js` filter row: default `hide`, one load per select change at `offset=0`, zero loads while typing and one after the pause, Enter without a second fire from the debounce, Clear back to `hide`, and the filter round-tripping through `localStorage`.

**Baseline:** the local suite has **15 pre-existing failures** that also fail on unmodified `main` — 8 websearch tests reading the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. Nothing to chase there.

`tests/core/test_request_log.py::test_stats_cache_evicts_least_recently_used` pinned the cache key's arity and was updated knowingly — that arity is the guard against exactly the bug above.

## Residual risks

- **Exports are unfiltered, deliberately.** The export window forwards the analytics filters, so `local` now rides along in the export query and is ignored server-side (verified: `/admin/api/export?...&local=hide` returns 200 and includes locally answered rows). An export therefore still contains everything. Stated in the Guide and `docs/USAGE.md` rather than widening this change into `api/export.py`.
- **All time / lifetime totals are unfiltered**, as they are for every other filter. The tab's own wording now says the cards and charts follow this filter and the rollup does not.
- The dashboard default is a behaviour change a returning user will notice: the cards drop from 14,662 to 13,326 on this install. Switching **Local answers** to **Show** restores the old totals, and the release notes lead with that.
- `provider=local:<rule>` combined with `local=hide` returns nothing — both predicates are ANDed. That is the honest answer to a contradictory question rather than silently dropping one; covered by a test.
- jsdom has no layout engine, so the new select's placement in the filter row was checked in Chrome by eye and by the a11y snapshot, not by an automated layout assertion.

## Not done

Retry, rotation, health and export behaviour untouched. No new env var, so `.env.example` (denied in this environment) was not needed and was not edited.

feat(analytics): hide locally answered requests by default, and apply filters as they change

The Analytics tab counted every request MCC answered itself alongside the ones
that actually went to a provider. On this machine that is 1,336 of 14,662 rows
(9%): 1,028 probe auto-responses, 278 title-generation skips, 30
suggestion-mode skips. They dominated the table's first page, sat in the
provider breakdown as `answered locally - <rule>`, and inflated every card,
chart and rate on the page, so "how is my proxy doing upstream" could not be
read off the tab without mentally subtracting them. The second complaint was
mechanical: changing a filter did nothing until Apply was clicked, so the
numbers on screen routinely answered a question the controls no longer asked.

Locally answered rows are exactly `provider IS NULL AND optimization IS NOT
NULL`; `provider IS NULL AND optimization IS NULL` is the `(unknown)` case and
is a different claim, so it stays visible. One `_where()` serves list, stats
and pulse, so a single predicate there covers the table, the cards, the series
and model charts, the provider/key breakdowns, top errors and the
fallback/diverted routes at once.

`local` takes `all` / `hide` / `only`; absent means `all`, so no existing
caller moves - exports, curl and the Guide's examples see what they always saw.
Only the dashboard defaults to `hide`, and it is `local` in the stats cache key
that keeps a "hide" call inside the 5 s TTL from being served the "all" numbers
it just cached. Every filter control now reloads from page 1 and persists:
selects on `change`, the text boxes 400 ms after the last keystroke, Enter
still immediate, Clear back to the defaults including Hide. Apply stays for
people who would rather press it; `loadId` already discards stale responses, so
overlapping loads from fast typing settle on the last one.

Verification (this worktree's server on 8099 over a `VACUUM INTO` copy of the
real 14,662-row log; the user's 8082 and ~/.fcc untouched, read-only):

  hide         13,326        0                              6 (no local:*)

    /admin/api/requests?limit=25&offset=0&status=error&local=hide (offset reset)

  all -> hide -> all inside 5 s: 14,662 / 13,326 / 14,662 (no cache-bypass
    flag needed - the filter is in the key, so a changed filter is a miss)
  pulse under auto-refresh: /admin/api/requests/pulse?local=only, no churn
  F5 -> filter still Only, 1,336. Zero console errors.

  uv run pytest -q --tb=line: 15 failed, 7723 passed, 38 skipped - the same 15
  that fail on unmodified main (8 websearch reading the real ~/.fcc/.env, 6
  PowerShell installer, test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache).
  ruff format / ruff check / ty check: all clean.
  jsdom (114 passed) drives the real admin.js: default `hide`, one load per
  select change at offset 0, one load per typing pause, Enter without a second
  fire, Clear back to `hide`, and the filter round-tripping through localStorage.

`test_stats_cache_evicts_least_recently_used` pinned the cache key's arity and
was updated knowingly - that arity is the guard against exactly this bug.

Not done: exports and the All time lifetime rollup stay unfiltered. The export
window forwards the analytics filters, so `local` now rides along in its query
and is ignored server-side; an export therefore still contains locally answered
